jobs.description: Legal-dong code changes from code.go.kr (root ADR-0143, ADR-0144), the collection half: first ask the site's own change-period filter which codes were created or abolished inside the window the last full run anchored (about 70 KB, root ADR-0322 §2); when it lists the same rows and no full reconcile is owed (code-go-kr-legal-dong.contract.json full_table.changed_since_probe), record the confirmation and stop. Otherwise land the full table (codes, parents, created and abolished dates) in Bronze (requests at least 15 seconds apart; the change-notice board is not a source), refuse a response whose shape changed or a table that shrank past the contract's bounds, record when the table was last confirmed, and, only when the table's rows changed, write a pending-load handoff. No Spark: lineage_stewardship loads and pairs the handoff under its spark slots before its own steps.
jobs.disk_measured: not measured: computed bound for a job whose command opens a DuckDB stage over tables of thousands to millions of rows (its stage database and staged files). The stage logs `duckdb stage closed: disk_bytes=<n>` as it closes (root ADR-0622); a pull request replaces this bound with the highest logged value, nothing is kept between runs.
jobs.disabled_reason: Paused for the Bronze epoch (root ADR-0626 §8 N2, W114, coordinator 2026-11-28): the writer of the code.go.kr table the epoch renames (codegokr__legal_dong_code) and re-keys. The job bronze_epoch moves those objects to the key today's writer builds and their ledger rows in place, and refuses while a writer of theirs has run in the last two close intervals; a run here meanwhile would split a source row or land a key of the old form. The resume pull request turns it on again (enabled true, enabled_since its merge) once the epoch's report is verified. Nothing is lost while it is off: a collector's next run asks what is due from its state and its Silver table, and a Silver load plans from the ledger what its table has not recorded. It was at dagster_stage dagster, where the resume puts it back. The deploy started it once (started_once_after_deploy), which the resume restores.

expected_outcome.no_change_bound_reason: Its provider publishes on no fixed day (expected_cadence `irregular` in docs/catalog/public-source-endpoint-catalog.v1.json), so a run that finds nothing new is healthy. That it keeps finishing is the done bound.
